intro: The first eight reviewed Pilot changes are merged into develop. A follow-up adds a minimal automatic-update switch in Settings > About. It is built and tested locally on feat/auto-update-ui.

details.Root cause: NginxConfig had http_port and https_port, but no config file fed them. A [nginx] table in bench.toml was ignored without a warning, so nginx always listened on 80 and 443.
details.Change: One nginx serves every bench on a host, so the ports are a host setting: [nginx] http_port and https_port in common_config.toml (defaults 80 and 443). Pilot checks the values and stops with a clear error when a value is bad. A [nginx] table in bench.toml is now an error that names common_config.toml. The admin readiness check reads the port from the same file. Two copies of the port-suffix code now use one helper, login.origin().
details.Tests: New tests: ports round trip, defaults are not written, bad ports fail, [nginx] in bench.toml fails. The admin readiness tests now set the port in common_config.toml. Earlier full suite: 4059 passed. Final checks are below.

details.Change: Settings > Bench has a common site config editor. The site editor uses the same component. Pick a known key or add a custom key with a type. The dialog uses 60% of the row for the key and 40% for the value. Long values are cut with an ellipsis.
details.Secrets: Password fields are write-only. The API returns a mask, never the stored value. Users can set or remove encryption_key. Only keys that Pilot writes are blocked.
details.Checks: Core, API and frontend tests cover config updates, types, managed keys and secret masking. The earlier test server run checked saves and rejected managed keys. The screenshots below show the final local review changes.

images.caption: Reviewed config table: known key labels, masked secrets and long values.
Reviewed add dialog: choose a known key and enter its typed value.

items.label: Merged

details.Why: The Settings > Database review found three display problems. The data and actions were correct.

In edit mode the card header cut '50 advised' to '50 adv…'. The note now leaves out the label (the icon stays): '1535 advised · up to 2128', or 'Use 10 to 87' in red for a bad value. 3. MariaDB shows 'no limit' as 2^64-1 bytes, and the list showed tmp_disk_table_size as '16777216 TB'. It now shows 'No limit'.

items.title: Update failed button blocks access to updates
items.label: Merged

details.Change: Dismiss closes a failed update, restarts services on the current code, restores the saved maintenance and scheduler settings, and deletes its backup. The Closed tab keeps the record. Restore skips apps and sites that were removed after the failure.
details.UI: The attention card has Retry, Skip patch, Restore backup and Dismiss. Each action has a short confirmation. Successful actions refresh the state.
details.Interruption checks: Two real migrates were force-stopped on the test server. Both paused safely in Needs attention. Dismiss restored maintenance_mode and pause_scheduler. A task stopped after its migrate step paused without a failed site, so Retry could finish the operation.
details.Issue #600: The separate Update code & retry action was removed at review. The chosen path is Dismiss, then start a new update. Dismiss deletes the original backup and lets sites run again. A later backup can therefore contain a partly migrated database.

images.caption: Reviewed attention card after a simulated failed local update.

items.title: Keep the pre-update backup in the S3 bucket
items.label: Merged

details.Change: With a bench bucket and [s3] upload_migration_backups enabled, each MariaDB table dump streams through gzip into S3. Restore streams each object through gunzip into MariaDB. No database dump is written to local disk. The table list, config copy and S3 location stay local.
details.Settings: The switch is in Settings > Bench. It is on by default and ignored without a bucket. SQLite and PostgreSQL backups stay local. The disk check counts only sites that back up locally.
details.Safety: A failed dump deletes its object. Restore checks that all objects exist before it starts imports. Dismiss and discard delete this backup's objects.
details.S3 fixes: Custom endpoints use path-style requests to avoid bucket hostname TLS errors. Settings reports TLS errors and keeps a custom region.
details.Checks: The test server backed up 30 tables to the test bucket. Restore recovered the site and its old app commit, then removed the backup. After review, focused tests checked streamed restore with no local dump file. The final switch location is in the reviewed source; the earlier storage screenshot was removed.

items.title: Send all notifications to webhooks, with an event filter per endpoint
items.label: Merged

details.Configuration: Endpoints use the top-level [[webhook_endpoints]] array in common_config.toml. Each has a URL, an optional token and events. An empty event list receives every event. Old entries under resource_limits still load and move on the next save.
details.Delivery: Each endpoint receives a fixed JSON body. A token adds Bearer authorization and an HMAC-SHA256 signature in X-Pilot-Signature-256. Safe task context is included. Passwords, tokens and repository URLs are excluded.
details.Events: Webhooks receive site, backup, app, update, Pilot and certificate events. They also receive site recovery and resource recovery events. Mail and Central receive alerts only.
details.UI: Settings > Notifications has an event picker, an optional token and a Test button. Save changes is at the right of the card.
details.Checks: Earlier live tests checked signed delivery, filters, test requests and delivery errors. Unit and frontend checks cover the expanded event set and the new top-level config. The earlier screenshots show the picker and Test button before the last layout review.

images.caption: Settings > Notifications: optional token, events per endpoint, and the Test button result.
The event picker. No choice means all events.

items.title: Validate alerting: alerts on by default, and each alert checked end to end
items.label: Merged

details.Default alerts: CPU, memory and disk alerts were off on every host. They now start at 90%, and site uptime stays on. The enable_default_alerts patch turns them on once on an older host that had all three off. On the test server the patch changed 0/0/0 to 90/90/90. A host that set any limit keeps its values.
details.Central bug: Central's report_pilot_event refuses an event type that is not one of its Server types. Pilot sent site_down, but Central calls it site_unavailable, so a managed host's team never got site-down alerts. Pilot now sends Central's names: site_down → site_unavailable, backups_failing → backup_failure, a failed update → migration_failure, and resource_limit_breached as it is. Central has no certificate type, so certificate_expiry goes to mail and webhooks only. Checked against Central's develop fixtures; not sent to a real Central.
details.Less noise: Mail and Central get only alerts. Each failed backup attempt was going to be a task mail (6 a day). Now an inbox gets one 'Backups of <site> are failing' mail, and every task event still goes to webhooks and the feed.
details.Better bodies: Resource, site-down and certificate alerts now carry a title, category, severity, site and dashboard link. The mail subject uses the title, so it names the site.
details.Live test: On the test server: an SMTP sink with a real TLS certificate (STARTTLS checked) and a webhook receiver that checks the signature. Limits set to 1-5%, web workers stopped, and a site's DB password broken. Mail and webhook both got: Resource limit breached (after 5 minutes), '2 sites are unreachable', and 'Backups of <site> are failing' (once, at the 6th failure). The feed got each one. Then the server was restored.
details.Found, not changed: The uptime ping (/api/method/ping) does not use the database, so a site with a broken DB still counts as up.
details.Tests: New tests: the patch (all off, any set, runs once, no common config), the Central name for each event, a failed task skips mail and Central, a certificate alert is mailed but not sent to Central, the site-down title for one or more sites, and the payload fields.

images.caption: Settings > Notifications on a host after the patch: every alert on, at 90%.

items.title: Custom domain and TLS status from the certificate on disk
items.label: Merged

details.Scope: On your note, there are no WHOIS, RDAP, DNS or HTTP checks. Pilot never connects to a domain, so a Sleepy VM stays asleep. All state comes from the certificate files and certbot's results.
details.Root cause: A failed issue or renewal was only printed in the task log. The domain list showed a plain lock, so a broken domain looked the same as one waiting for a certificate.
details.Change: bench.certificates keeps one record per certificate in logs/certificates.json: the names asked for, the names the file covers, the expiry, and certbot's last error. Each obtain records its result, and the daily certificate timer reads each file again. Certbot now writes its output to the task log, and a failure keeps certbot's reason (Domain, Type, Detail) instead of a generic footer.
details.Domain status: valid, pending, failed, expiring (under 14 days, so renewal is not working) or expired. The last three mean the domain is broken. A new domain that fails does not mark the names the current file still covers as broken. A renewal failure inside the 30-day window marks every name as failed.
details.Alerts: A certificate that breaks raises one certificate_failed or certificate_expiry alert to the feed, mail and webhooks. Pilot alerts again only after the certificate was valid and then broke again.
details.Test server: Port 80 was blocked for one minute and a new domain was added. Certbot failed, the domain showed 'Certificate failed' with certbot's reason, and one signed certificate_failed webhook arrived. A second failed run did not alert again. With port 80 open, the timer added the domain to the certificate, both domains showed valid, and the alert was reset.
details.Tests: New tests: each state, a failed new domain does not break covered names, a new domain waits, a success clears the failure, alert once until valid again, issue failure recorded and alerted, the domain row status, certbot's reason kept, and the UI badge and tooltip. Tests never shell out to sudo for certificate files.
details.Review UI: The final screenshot uses simulated API responses in the real dashboard to show every state. It is not live certificate evidence. An expiring certificate currently has a red open lock, even while HTTPS still works.

images.caption: Real dashboard with simulated valid, expiring, expired, failed and pending certificates.

items.title: Automatic Pilot updates in Settings > About
items.label: Built locally

details.UI: One default Frappe UI switch below the Pilot version. It saves immediately. Checks run daily at 12:00 AM UTC for all benches. There is no time picker.
details.Source installs: The switch is disabled and says Unavailable for source installs. The API also rejects changes on a source install.
details.Save errors: The switch keeps its previous value and shows the error. A failed cron change keeps the stored setting. Concurrent changes use the common config lock.
details.Checks: 41 focused backend and cron tests pass. Three browser tests, type checking and the dashboard build pass. The UTC guard is checked at midnight and at other times, with a non-UTC server timezone. Upgrade tests cover disabled hosts, repeated runs and a failed cron change.
details.Branch: feat/auto-update-ui. Built locally; no Pilot commit or pull request yet.
details.Screens: The real dashboard uses simulated release and source-install responses here. These previews do not change the host cron job.
details.Schedule: A short cron command checks the UTC clock each minute. It starts Pilot only at midnight UTC. The server timezone does not change this time. An upgrade patch replaces the old schedule only on hosts where automatic updates are already on.

Source install: the switch is disabled with a short explanation.
